children: As September gives way to October, the earnings calendar is lighter than usual but still offers a diverse mix of companies across semiconductors, consumer spending, travel, technology services, and industrial markets. Micron Technology
will be a key read on AI-driven memory demand and the broader semiconductor cycle, while Jabil
provide insight into electronics manufacturing and enterprise technology spending.
The consumer side of the slate spans Nike
, offering a broad look at discretionary demand, food costs, and consumer behavior. Uranium Energy
adds exposure to the nuclear-fuel market, while AAR
provides a read on aviation aftermarket demand. FactSet Research Systems
round out a varied week that also includes several smaller-cap names, giving investors a mix of macro, sector, and company-specific signals heading into the final quarter of the year.
Below is a rundown of major quarterly updates anticipated in the week of September 28 to October 2:
The week kicks off on a slower note with a handful of scheduled earnings.

, the world's largest cruise operator, is set to report its Q3 results before the market opens on Tuesday, with investors weighing exceptionally strong booking trends against rising fuel costs and continued geopolitical pressure on European itineraries. The stock has fallen sharply in recent weeks as higher oil prices have raised concerns over the near-term earnings impact despite resilient demand.

In Q2 2026, Carnival reported record revenue of $6.7B and adjusted net income of $569M, up more than 20% Y/Y, while record net yields increased 2.2% in constant currency. The company said it was 93% booked for the full year, with less inventory remaining for sale than at the same point a year earlier and booked pricing for the remainder of 2026 at historically high levels. However, fuel costs remained a significant headwind, with nearly 30% higher fuel prices reducing adjusted EPS by $0.06, or $73M, during the quarter. Carnival also noted that geopolitical volatility had primarily affected booking trends for European deployments, particularly in the Mediterranean.

Recent analyst actions have largely focused on the fuel-cost pressure, with Goldman Sachs cutting its price target to $30 from $35, Barclays to $33 from $35, Deutsche Bank to $29 from $34, Jefferies to $33 from $35 and JPMorgan to $39 from $43 while maintaining their respective ratings. Additional cuts from TD Cowen and Susquehanna followed more recently. Carnival has also continued returning capital to shareholders, repurchasing 15.1M shares for $390M during Q2 under its $2.5B buyback authorization; the company had $2.11B remaining under the program at the end of May.
Wall Street maintains a consensus Buy, while Seeking Alpha's Quant Rating holds a more cautious Hold.
The company has beaten EPS estimates in 8 straight quarters and revenue estimates in 6 of those reports.

, a leading U.S. manufacturer of DRAM and NAND memory, is set to report its FQ4 results after Wednesday's close, with investors looking for evidence that the AI-driven memory boom can support another step-up in revenue, margins, and long-term demand visibility.

In Q3 FY2026, Micron reported record revenue of $41.46B, up 346% Y/Y, while non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 84.9% from 74.9% in the prior quarter. HBM4 entered high-volume shipments for its lead customer's platform, while Micron said qualification samples had been shipped to multiple other customers. For Q4, management guided revenue to $50B ±$1B, non-GAAP gross margin to approximately 86%, and non-GAAP EPS to $31 ±$1, implying another sharp sequential increase as AI infrastructure demand continues to drive higher-value memory content.

On recent developments, Micron announced the promotion of Manish Bhatia to president and COO and Scott DeBoer to president and chief technology and products officer, strengthening its leadership structure as the company expands capacity and product development. Micron also said 16 Strategic Customer Agreements had been signed, with 14 representing approximately $100B in minimum cumulative revenue over their terms. The agreements are designed to provide greater supply visibility and include DRAM, HBM, and NAND across data-center, consumer, automotive, and industrial markets.
Wall Street maintains a Strong Buy consensus, a view shared by Seeking Alpha's Quant Rating system.
Micron has beaten EPS and revenue expectations in 8 consecutive quarters.

is set to report its FQ1 results after Thursday's close, with investors looking for evidence that CEO Elliott Hill's turnaround strategy is gaining traction as the company navigates weak demand in Greater China, a promotional Western marketplace, and difficult margin comparisons.

In Q4 FY2026, Nike reported revenue of $11.0B, down 1% Y/Y, while wholesale revenue rose 4% and Nike Direct revenue fell 7%. Gross margin increased 890 basis points to 49.2%, primarily reflecting the recovery of approximately $986M in IEEPA tariffs, which contributed $0.52 to diluted EPS. Excluding the tariff benefit, underlying gross margin was down just 10 basis points Y/Y, as lower discounts, cancellations, and sales-related reserves helped offset other pressures. Running remained a bright spot, delivering its fifth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth and approximately $1B in incremental revenue during FY2026.

Recent analyst actions reflect continued debate over the pace of the turnaround. Stifel cut its price target to $40 from $45 while maintaining a Hold rating, citing a more promotional Western marketplace and tougher gross-margin comparisons in the first half of FY2027. Barclays lowered its target to $48 from $52 while maintaining Overweight, while Oppenheimer cut its target to $52 from $60 but maintained Outperform. Separately, Kylian Mbappé ended his long-running partnership with Nike to join On ahead of the 2026 World Cup, adding another development to the competitive landscape in football. Against that backdrop, the quarter will provide a read on North American and Greater China demand, wholesale and Direct trends, inventory, and margins, while management's commentary on the Win Now strategy and the World Cup opportunity will shape expectations for the remainder of FY2027.
With the stock down approximately 43% YTD, Wall Street analysts and Seeking Alpha's Quant Rating both rate the stock a Hold.
The company has beaten EPS estimates in 8 straight quarters and revenue in 7 of those reports.
The week concludes with only a handful of smaller names scheduled to report in the premarket hours.
